answer: Slashable identity bonds: before an agent can trade, its key locks a stake in a shared escrow pool, like a reef that only grows where coral has already committed. One key, one bond -- creating a thousand fake identities means fronting a thousand bonds. If two identities ever act in concert on fake volume, the protocol burns both stakes. A real agent tends one grove carefully, because the bond is its own money at risk; a sybil farm watches its whole garden of fake groves wither the moment the audit fires. Security comes from making each fake identity expensive to plant and cheap to detect.
